params.tagline: The intersection of form and function
params.intro: I am a plant anatomist and physiologist, studying how the structure of phloem, xylem and petioles shapes the way plants move carbon and water. I am particularly interested in two research questions, both of which I am actively pursuing. First, are there limits on phloem structure and function in petioles? Second, how does seasonality affect phloem structure and function?
params.intro_note: Currently, I work in environmental compliance and permitting.

research_highlights.title: Does drought season affect carbon transport in crop plants?
research_highlights.summary: Comparing spring, summer and fall droughts in Prunus, Populus and Quercus, alongside work on Citrus phloem and citrus greening.

research_highlights.title: How do petioles limit or enhance the movement of water and sugar?
research_highlights.summary: Vascular arrangement and packing in petioles, and what they mean for leaf physiology.
